title: AUTOHALLUSION: Automatic Generation of Hallucination Benchmarks for Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: The authors measure this bias by probing the language modules of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to identify strong object co-occurrence priors (cognitive schemas). They then manipulate images using three strategies—abnormal object insertion, paired object insertion, and correlated object removal—to create conflicts between the visual evidence and the model's language priors, and evaluate the hallucination rates through Visual Question Answering (VQA) focusing on object existence and spatial relations.
